title.narrative: Empowering Rural Communities of Vanuatu through Renewable Energy Solutions (Solar PV for Water, Education, and Health Centers)

description.narrative: The Empowering Rural Communities of Vanuatu through Renewable Energy Solutions project is designed to tackle critical gaps in energy and water access by integrating solar-powered infrastructure for water supply, healthcare, and education. This initiative will install solar water pumping systems at eight (8) sites across eight rural communities on the islands of Santo, Malekula, Paama, and Tanna, ensuring consistent access to clean water while eliminating reliance on costly and polluting diesel-powered pumps.To further strengthen community resilience, the project will equip twenty-four (24) health and education facilities with standalone solar PV systems and battery energy storage system (BESS). These installations will provide uninterrupted, sustainable electricity to power essential services, improving healthcare delivery, enhancing educational outcomes, and fostering long-term economic and social benefits for these communities. The 24 health and education systems will be located across the 8 community areas receiving solar water pumps through this initiative as well in additional communities who have previously received solar water pumps through GGGI’s previous SWPS Phase I & II project. In doing so this REnew Pacific investment ensures a holistic energy solution across primary services for these communities.

This idea is to implement learnings from from the Phase II - Scaling-up Climate Resilience through Solar-Powered Direct Water Access project. It involves scaling up from the 'Scaling-up Climate Resilience through Solar-Powered Direct Water Access' in Vanuatu. The Empowering Rural Communities of Vanuatu through Renewable Energy Solutions project aims to address critical energy and water access challenges in rural Vanuatu through the deployment of solar-powered solutions. The initiative will install solar water pumping systems in eight rural communities on the islands of Santo, Malekula, Paama, and Tanna, while also equipping twenty-four (24) health and education facilities with standalone solar photovoltaic (PV) systems integrated with battery energy storage systems. The initiative incorporates a community and government-led governance model, ensuring long-term sustainability through training, local participation, and access to concessional finance and technical support.List of Site Names:LiroNaluken 1 & 2Port ResolutionSaralokambuBetervatLeerongrongTahiVaoleli
